Commentary.Commentary: Hey, wait! Where are you going? Blockbuster Sunday has just begun! This final was just a starter. The main course comes in a few minutes from now when England take on India in the third T20I! Do catch that game and have a great Sunday! ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

A bit of a break for Australia now. They go back home and then head to the Middle East to face the same opposition, Pakistan - this time for a tougher contest - Tests, ODIs and T20Is. Pakistan, meanwhile, have an ODI series against Zimbabwe not too far away.

Okay! That ends a tri-series which lasted a week. Pakistan strut their stuff, albeit after a nervy start. Australia stay winless in terms of series - lost both the ODI and T20I series in England and now, having done reasonably well in the league stages, stuttering in the final. Aaron Finch's Melbourne side is not too different in knockout matches in the Australian T20 League - nerve loss in the final? Perhaps.

Victorious captain, Sarfraz Ahmed, says that the win is due to a great team effort. First the bowlers bowled well at the death and then with the bat, Malik and Zaman took them across the line. Admits that the fielding let them down but he had confidence in his team's batting, in spite of chasing down 184 which is not an easy task. Praises Fakhar Zaman for his innings, stressing that he has played well throughout the series. Has good words of praise for his unit, and says it is not easy to play 6 games in 8 days (actually 5). On the ODI series further against Zimbabwe, he feels that is it not easy to play against Zimbabwe in Zimbabwe and hopes that his team puts on a good show.

MAN OF THE MATCH AND SERIES, FAKHAR ZAMAN, says that he likes these pitches in Zimbabwe. Further says that he was in form from the very first game. Informs us that he toured the country in 2016, but did not perform well then. In this series, the wickets were really good, he feels. On being asked about the plan to go about the run chase, he blatantly says that he told the team that he will play his own game, rest all play around him. Praises Australia for putting on a good show and credits his team for winning the trophy. On the future, he says that he needs to work hard and maintain his consistency and form.

Aussie captain, Aaron Finch admits that Australia should have got to 200 with the bat. Praises Pakistan for bowling well towards the end, which resulted in his side losing wickets. Feels that the wicket looked on the slower side. Says that the Aussies started off really well with the ball. But also says that Zaman played exceedingly well and took it away from them.

Do not forget - Pakistan bowled well at the death, 'restricting' Australia to 183, when at one stage, 200 seemed likely. The Men In Yellow could not replicate that with the ball. Zaman's wicket and Tye's excellent 17th over gave Australia a glimmer of hope - but reliable Malik took them over the line easily. Nothing much to talk about the Aussie bowling - Jhye Richardson and Billy Stanlake were economical but not incisive. Maxwell, of course, picked up 2 wickets. Stay tuned for the presentation.

Zaman should be called the Man Of The Finals.  If anyone does remember, he pulverized India in the 2017 Champions Trophy final, batting first. Today, he made 91 in a run chase. He received good support or mentorship from Shoaib Malik. They seized the moment perfectly. Jack Wildermuth came on to bowl the 11th over and suddenly, in the span of 3 overs, Pakistan had scored 48 runs. That changed the momentum.

This is PAKISTAN'S HIGHEST SUCCESSFUL RUN CHASE IN T20IS, but by no means was it perfectly planned. They lost 2 wickets to Maxwell in the opening over and then, after a bit of a fightback, lost Sarfraz too. But a terrific 107-run stand in 64 balls between Fakhar Zaman and Shoaib Malik completely turned the tables.

9th series win on the trot in T20Is for Pakistan. They last lost a series, or failed to win one, when Daren Sammy's Windies, known as West Indies then, took the WT20 trophy in 2016. Since then, a change of captaincy, some change in personnel and boy - we have a world-beating side!

World Number 1 team. They have strut their stuff. Looked like luck was not on their side. Seemed like the target was too big for them. Felt like they were going to lose by a big margin when they lost 2 wickets in the opening over. But, the man for the finals - Fakhar Zaman and Mr. Never-Forget-Me Consistent, Shoaib Malik, ensured that Pakistan kept their winning run intact, in terms of series victories.

FOUR! PAKISTAN ARE THE CHAMPIONS! A short ball, on middle and off, Asif pulls it over mid-wicket. There is a man in the deep but he cannot get to the ball in time and it beats him to the fence! Congratulations, Pakistan!
Full on middle, heaved through mid on for a single.
Marcus Stoinis to bowl an over which could last a solitary ball.

Full on middle, Asif drives this down to long on. He takes a single but Malik calls him back for the second. The fielder returns a decent throw to the keeper but Asif dives in. Andrew Tye finishes a fruitless spell as well - 4-0-33-0.
Full toss on middle, paddle swept to fine leg for a run.
Slower ball, outside off, Malik looks to cut but gets a bottom edge which goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Full on middle, pushed down to long on for a run.
The batsman works it down the leg side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
FOUR! Just over! A length ball outside off, Malik backs away and slices this over point. The fielder leaps but in vain! Just 7 more needed from 12 balls!

SIX! CLUNK! That seals the deal. It really should. Pakistan's game to lose from here. A length ball on middle, Asif backs away and hits it miles over long on! Richardson is on his haunches - 2-0-6-0 at one stage - only to end up with 4-0-29-1. 17 runs came from his final over.
Goes back and heaves this slower ball past the bowler to long on. Finch puts in a good sliding stop rushing to his left and keeps the batsmen to a couple.
A short ball, on middle, pulled through mid-wicket for a run.
A slower ball outside off, Ali waits for it and drives it to long off for a run. The stand moves to 10 from 9 balls.
Finch has a chat with Jhye - the latter looks very nervous.
Very full, on middle, driven down to long on for a single.

SIX! CLUBBED! Malik releases the pressure! A short ball, outside off, Shoaib hangs back and pulls it massively over mid-wicket! That will put pressure on the bowler. Malik moves to 34 from 30 balls, with his first six.
Outside off, Ali swings but misses. A crucial over from Tye - just 2 coming from it.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Gets some sense, pushes the ball to long off for a single. Pakistan can do it in singles and twos. No risks needed. 29 more needed from 20 balls.
Outside off, another slash and a miss.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, Ali looks to steer it to third man but misses. The keeper and bowler appeal but in vain.
Asif Ali is the new man in while Andrew Tye is the change-in bowler.

OUT! Zaman does not get a century! But guess he has done enough to see his team through to yet another series win. A short ball on middle, Zaman backs away, like he has been doing all innings and upper cuts this. But finds substitute Nic Maddinson to perfection. He has missed out on a well-deserving ton. But his team has a hand on the trophy - unless, a Steve Waugh type Australianism can prevail. Just 30 more needed from 24 balls.
Angling in, from outside off, worked through mid-wicket for a run.
A short ball, extra bounce, Fakhar adjusts nicely and punches it towards point for a run.
Waits for the ball to come to him and dabs it to third man for a single.
Outside off, played straight to point.
WIDE. Slower ball gone awry, down the leg side, Malik misses his flick.
Full on middle, worked wide of long on for a couple.
Jhye Richardson is back on. 2-0-6-0 so far. Last ray of hope for the Aussies - if any.

MISFIELD, FOUR! Australia are going down and going down very badly. A short ball outside off, Zaman punches it towards sweeper cover. Ashton Agar comes running in but then slips and the ball spins away from him, to the fence behind! 12 from the over, Stoinis has gone for 26 in his 2 overs. THE 100-RUN STAND IS UP, in just 58 balls. Fakhar punches his fists with the air - looking at Malik. Finch said that Australia have saved their best for the last - well, he might have misspelt Pakistan I guess. Just 36 more needed from 30 balls.
FOUR! Fine shot. Another slower ball, outside off, Fakhar stands tall and punches it through the covers for a boundary!
A slower bouncer, on middle, Malik swivels and pulls it towards fine leg for another one.
A full toss outside off, squeezed towards Aaron Finch at extra cover for one.
On middle and leg, heaved to fine leg for a run.
Short and outside off, slapped to deep cover for a single.
Marcus Stoinis is being brought back on. Was hammered for 14 in his first over.
Full on middle and leg, driven back to the bowler. Stanlake is done and dusted with - nothing today - 4-0-25-0. Was economical, but Australia needed him to do what he did on Monday.
Around off, a backfoot defense. A DOT BALL AFTER 19 LEGAL DELIVERIES!
A length ball, following the batsman down the leg side, FZ swings but the ball goes off the inner half of his blade towards mid-wicket. A run taken. Moves to 80 from 40 balls.

SIX! CLOBBERED! Bring out the short stuff, says Fakhar! This is on middle, Zaman backs away and smashes it way over the point fence! Aussie bowlers are stunned - they don't know what has hit them. Not too long ago, they were on top. In a matter of minutes, they are being squashed down. Just 49 more needed from 39 balls now.
Outside off, steered behind point for a run.
They are not getting any with that line. Full toss, way down the leg side, luckily for them, Zaman misses his flick and the ball goes off his pads fine. A leg bye taken.
Billy Stanlake is back on. 3-0-17-0 so far. Australia desperately need a wicket or two.
Full and outside off, pushed through mid off for a run. The stand moves to 80 from 46 balls. 15 from the over, 48 from the last 3!
Outside off, calmly pushed to point for a quick run. Moves to 20 from 19 balls - do not forget his contribution in this partnership. Was dropped on 0 though.

TOP EDGE, FOUR! Luck finally coming back to Pakistan. A short ball, on middle, Malik swivels, looks to pull but is done in by the pace. Gets a top edge which flies over the keeper to the fine leg fence! 59 more needed now, from 44 balls! At this rate, they might win with an over or two to spare...
Full and outside off, pushed towards mid off for a quick single.

FOUR! That is a stamping authority to what was mentioned on ball number 1. Favourites. A short ball, Zaman swivels and pulls it behind square leg for consecutive boundaries! Zaman moves to 71 from 35 balls, with his 10th four! The stand is worth 73 from 42 deliveries.

FOUR! Edged away! Tye will not like that, but remember, the Aussies got majority of their shots in that fashion. On a length outside off, angling away, Zaman looks to run it down to third man but is too close to the ball. Ends up getting a thick outside edge which flies past the keeper and beats short third man to the fence! 68 more needed from 47 balls now as Pakistan are now clear favourites.
Andrew Tye is back on. 1-0-7-0 so far.
Full and wide outside off, Fakhar swings but misses. The keeper is not able to stop it and the ball goes off his pads to short third man. A bye taken. 17 from the over, 33 from the last 2!

FOUR! And again! A hat-trick of shots in that region. Pakistan are demolishing Agar's figures and morale here. One more flighted ball, one more dancing step, one more connection of bat with ball and the latter flies to the long on fence.
FOUR! He goes again! Comes down the track and hammers it well down the ground, with long on being a mere spectator!
SIX! BRUTAL! The target is Ashton Agar. Zaman puts on his dancing shoes and clubs it over long on! Gets to his half century - 4th in T20Is - crucially, consecutive ones for him!
On middle and off, eased through the covers for a run. 50-run stand is up as well.
Full on middle, hit down to long on for a single.
Ashton Agar time.
This would have been a wide as well but Fakhar goes after this one and crunches it through the covers for a run. 16 from the over! Pakistan need 89 from 54 balls.
Finally bat to ball. Punched towards point who has a needless shy at the bowler's end and concedes an overthrow. Australia losing the plot now. A bit careless on the field they are.

HAT-TRICK OF WIDES! Well, the youngster is a bit afraid of bowling it on the pads, simply because the field is set on the off side. But he does need to bowl a legal ball, doesn't he? Another one well outside off.
ANOTHER WIDE. Same formula, same result.
WIDE. Action replay of what happened a couple of balls agao. Batsman walks across, bowler bowls it wider from him, but well outside the guideline.
FOUR! Short and wide outside off, Zaman flays it through point and gets a boundary!
WIDE. Harsh on the bowler. He sees Zaman walk across the stumps and bowls it well outside off. But it is way beyond the guidelines and is wided.
Outside off, a slash and a miss.
On middle and leg, flicked away for a single. 100 more needed from 58 balls now.
FOUR! Loose start. Full and down the leg side, flicked behind square leg for a boundary. Malik is too good a player to miss out on freebies.
Jack Wildermuth comes into the attack.
Full and straight, driven straight to Jack Wildermuth at extra cover who fumbles and allows the ball to go through. Two runs taken.
Outside off, punched to deep point for a run.
Full and down the leg side, flicked straight to fine leg for a single. There are 4 men at the boundary on the off side. He can tuck the ball anywhere on the leg side and get a couple.
Very good ball. Zaman is already down the leg side, backing away and Stanlake follows him. Dishes in a bouncer and the batsman has to duck out of the way.
Full on middle, pushed down to long on for a single. 109 more needed from 64 balls.
Outside off, a flay and a miss.
Billy Stanlake is back on.
FOUR! Down the leg side, Zaman swings it behind square leg and gets a boundary! 11 from the over, 25 from the last 2!
The batsman has driven it through mid on. One run added to the total.
Pushes this through mid on for a run.
Comes down the track, Maxwell fires it in, outside off, Shoaib is caught off-guard but manages to push it past the keeper, off the bottom edge. A single to short third man.
Short and outside off, Malik cuts it through point. Backward point dives to his left and makes a half-stop. Short third man dives as well and makes another half-stop. A couple in the end.
Full on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a couple. 119 more needed from 71 balls.
Glenn Maxwell is back into the attack.
A short ball, pulled away, wide of Andrew Tye at short mid-wicket for one. 14 from the opening over of Stoinis.
A short ball, pulled through mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman has played it to the point region. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
Short and outside off, Fakhar looks to cut but the ball never arrives. Goes off the outside edge and lands in front of the keeper.
FOUR! A poor ball, short and down the leg side, Zaman helps it past short fine leg!
SIX! BOSH! A length ball, on middle and leg, Zaman swings this cleanly over mid-wicket!
Marcus Stoinis comes on to bowl.
Plays this straight to point. Just a single from that over.
The batsman guides it to third man.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
Outside off, steered to third man for a single.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Excellent yorker, well dug out.
On middle, Shoaib looks to tuck but misses and is hit on the box.

DROPPED! Full and outside off, Malik lofts this straight back. Tye leaps but is not able to catch that. Parries it to mid off. The fielder cannot get there either. Slice of luck. Can Malik make use of it?
Punches this off the back foot.
The batsman plays a pull shot to this short delivery. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Shoaib Malik is the new man in.

OUT! RUN OUT! My word - this is - excellent fielding from Australia. Flashback 1998 - why so far? Because that dismissal is fresh in my mind and though it is not exactly similar, it does bring out the brilliance in fielding. The then Zimbabwe captain, Alistair Campbell, had run a ball down to third man where Ajit Agarkar was fielding. He started to take a single but it was more of a stroll - Agarkar threw the ball from that position at the bowler's end - and hit the stumps! Campbell was short! Now, let us come back to the present. Campbell is a commentator now but somewhere in his mind, he might be remembering his dismissal in 1998. Sarfraz gets across and paddles it through fine leg. Jhye Richardson gets to the ball from deep square leg, slides and pulls the ball back in. Both batsmen turn blind for the third - and here is where the best part of the fielding comes - Richardson does not throw it to the keeper. He understands that Sarfraz has started to run only after he has picked up the ball and throws it to the bowler who disturbs the stumps! Sarfraz hangs around a touch - just to check whether Richardson had touched the ropes while fielding the ball - nope, luck is not his side. Timely wicket for Australia.
FOUR! Welcome into the attack! A length ball on middle, Sarfraz heaves this over mid on and gets a boundary! 139 more needed from 89 balls.
Andrew Tye to bowl now.
Tucks this through fine leg and gets a run. Good over from Jhye.
FOUR! Finally he connects this time. On a length outside off, Sarfraz backs away and smashes it over cover for a boundary.
'AAARGH!' yells Sarfraz in frustration. Fourth dot ball on the trot. A length ball outside off, Ahmed flays hard but misses.
Follows the batsman, who is backing down the leg side, trying a super innovative shot - a run down to third man with a slip in place -  only to miss.

Is that out? Nope. On a length outside off, moving away, Sarfraz has a cheeky poke, trying to run this down to third man but misses. The Aussie keeper goes up in an appeal, along with his mate at first slip but umpire Tiffin shakes his head. There does not seem to be any edge from the replays.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
The experiment is over. Jhye Richardson is into the attack now.
Pushes this through mid on for a run. 10 from that over, 31 off the last 2!

FOUR! Well done again. A short ball, Sarfraz making a statement here - that they will not be intimidated by the short stuff. Clubs a pull over mid-wicket and finds the fence. 149 more needed from 97 balls.
Outside off, on a length, Sarfraz swings but misses.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Outside off, punched to point for a quick single. Direct hit at the striker's end could have had Sarfraz back in the hut.
FOUR! He is doing a Short - chancing his arm. Not a bad ploy on this pitch. A short ball outside off, Zaman backs away and slices it high in the air. Manages to clear cover and gets a boundary.

FOUR! Where is Akash Chopra? Is he following this game? He must be sitting on his sofa somewhere and smiling -  saying to himself - 'Finchy, I would never have given Maxwell another over'. 21 have come from it and Pakistan have wrestled the momentum back from Australia. This is short and outside off, Sarfraz backs away and cuts it behind point for a boundary. 158 more needed from 102 balls.
SIX! Sarfraz is turning it on now! Full and outside off, Sarfraz gets down and mows it miles over mid-wicket!
Comes down the track, has a bit of a heave and the ball goes off the inner half towards mid on. A quick single taken.
FOUR! Nicely done! Floated outside off, Zaman backs away and lofts it over cover for consecutive boundaries! 169 more needed from 105 balls.
FOUR! BOOM! Full on middle, Zaman charges out and blasts it past the bowler through mid on for a boundary!

NEARLY HIS THIRD WICKET! Maxwell is causing some problems out there. He senses Zaman to charge and flights it outside off, slowing the pace down a bit. Zaman swings hard and gets a leading edge. Luckily for him, the ball lands beyond cover. Two runs taken.

Maxwell continues... if you go by Akash Chopra's instincts, this is a big risk. You normally bowl a part-timer only once in the Powerplay - bowling him for more than 1 over could be asking for trouble.
A short ball, around middle, Sarfraz looks to pull but the ball goes over the stumps.
Taps and runs it towards cover for a quick single. 179 more needed from 109 balls.

A bouncer at the head of the batsman, Zaman looks to play a belated pull - he first ducks, then attempts the shot - only to miss. He was out caught behind, trying to play the hook shot against Stanlake itself, in the first encounter.
Outside off, Ahmed drives this away from the body and gets a thick outside edge behind point to third man. A single taken.
Tighter line, towards the stumps, the keeper captain blocks.
Landed outside off, a touch wide, Sarfraz tamely pushes and misses.

What a tactic from Aaron Finch to give Glenn Maxwell the opening over. Totally caught Pakistan off guard. Credit to Maxwell too for not bowling it too loose. It will be a proper bowler from the other end - Billy Stanlake.
Landed short and outside off, cut away square on the off side but straight to the fielder. 3 runs and 2 wickets off the opening over, Maxwell has done a stupendous job.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single. Sarfraz is off the mark.
Sarfraz Ahmed, the skipper, is the next man in.

OUT! Second of the over for Maxwell! This is a dream start for Australia. Superb bowling. The slowness of the surface is showing already. He tosses it up around off, a hint of spin and that's all that's needed to get Talat. He plays the expansive drive away from his body and slices it towards backward point. Richardson there gobbles it up with ease. No trouble there.
Not much spin on this occasion, fuller and around off, Talat pushes it to the covers.
Quicker through the air outside off, Talat plays and misses.
Hussain Talat walks in at no.3.

OUT! The debutant is gone! A horrifying start to his Pakistan career. Oh, dear. Maxwell darts it down the leg side as Farhan steps out of his crease a bit. Tries flicking it, misses and as he's attempting to get back, loses his balance and can't make it back in time as his leg gets stuck just before the crease. Carey takes the bails off in a flash. No need to go to the third umpire, the decision is that clear.
Full and on off from around the wicket, Zaman drives it to the right of mid off for a single. He's off the mark.

We are back for the chase. It's all set up for a belter if Pakistan can get going. On a rather slow surface, it will be Fakhar Zaman and the debutant Sahibzada Farhan to open the innings, with Glenn Maxwell taking the new ball first. Let's roll...
